newProbeMatrixAtoN.name: task-specific factory capability profiles
newProbeMatrixAtoN.evidence: A validation-role branch (validation/researchops-factory-v1-1-v3-015 onto correction-v3-014) is granted the SAME implementation-write privilege as a correction task: modifying lib/boundary.mjs, lib/lineage.mjs and the workflow all pass the boundary (ok=true). Factory role does not constrain capability.

newProbeMatrixAtoN.name: self-modifying validator / trusted-base enforcement
newProbeMatrixAtoN.evidence: A PR head may modify lineage.mjs + boundary.mjs (ok=true) and, because GitHub `pull_request` runs the checked-out head code, be validated by its own weakened boundary. There is no trusted/base enforcement root that cannot be self-authorized by the PR under check.

newProbeMatrixAtoN.name: exact commit/ancestry binding
newProbeMatrixAtoN.evidence: trustedModeFromMeta decides factory governance from the (head,base) branch-name pair only (no SHA input; arity 0). Head-descendant/base-tip commit ancestry is not verified; force-moved/reused branch names with unrelated history would pass; recovery no-op commits are silently trusted.

newProbeMatrixAtoN.name: current task record immutability
newProbeMatrixAtoN.evidence: The current task's own setup files are mutable and arbitrary extras are allowed: modifying correction-v3-validation-015/VALIDATION_CONTRACT.md (ok=true) and adding ARBITRARY_EXTRA.json (ok=true) both pass. Authorization is prefix-only over the whole result directory.

newProbeMatrixAtoN.name: future-task lineage preauthorization
newProbeMatrixAtoN.evidence: FACTORY_LINEAGE already contains the future validation-015 branch, so a future task is pre-authorized without an owner-created governance record. Entries are branch strings + resultDir only — no task id, issue/PR identity, role or allowed-file inventory.

newProbeMatrixAtoN.name: exact skeleton content, not filenames
newProbeMatrixAtoN.evidence: checkStageTransition creation compares the changed FILENAME set only (ok=true for the exact names) with no canonical byte/template check. An unsafe content substitution (e.g. a DEEP_RESEARCH_PROMPT.md stripped of official-source/no-production constraints, or added production-authorization language) in a valid-named file would pass the boundary.

newProbeMatrixAtoN.name: stage transition completeness
newProbeMatrixAtoN.evidence: A marker added to a non-open stage is rejected, and boundary+final validate jointly gate transitions (partial capture fails validate; wrong-stage adds fail boundary). NOTE: OWNER_CLOSEOUT_REQUIRED has no separate marker-add inventory (by design).

newProbeMatrixAtoN.name: marker protocol compatibility
newProbeMatrixAtoN.evidence: The validation enum omits governed outcomes (VALIDATED_WITH_NONBLOCKING_NOTES is rejected), so a strict validator can reject the factory's own governed output; and marker identity is accepted via a validationTaskId/correctionTaskId fallback rather than being bound strictly to the root research task id. Conflicting/unknown outcome keys are not detected.

newProbeMatrixAtoN.name: real merge record verification
newProbeMatrixAtoN.evidence: A merge record with mergeCommit = 40 zeros (and valid target/state/receipt fields) is ACCEPTED. There is no check that the merge commit exists in the repository, is reachable from main, that the receipt is linked by hash/immutable identifier, that the receipt predates the merge, or that main contains the governed task tree.

newProbeMatrixAtoN.name: owner receipt full lifecycle
newProbeMatrixAtoN.evidence: Only an exact research-record merge receipt passes; a factoryMergeToMainAuthorized escalation is rejected. NOTE: the validator does not require an explicit all-false non-merge authorization matrix to be present, and there is no post-merge receipt-immutability lifecycle check.

newProbeMatrixAtoN.name: history semantics and timestamps
newProbeMatrixAtoN.evidence: Timestamps are compared lexicographically, so non-ISO but lexicographically-ordered strings (aaa < bbb) pass; duplicate same-state entries pass; there is no governed history event-type/identity schema.

newProbeMatrixAtoN.name: actual NUL-delimited Git diff parser
newProbeMatrixAtoN.evidence: Against real `git -c core.quotePath=false diff -z --name-status` output: A d/added.txt, D 'd/na me.txt' (space preserved, unquoted), R100 d/oldname.txt->d/newname.txt (src+dst), M d/normal.txt — 4 records, none malformed; synthetic R101 and truncated R100 rejected.

newProbeMatrixAtoN.name: task root / filesystem identity
newProbeMatrixAtoN.evidence: A lowercase task id is not matched as a governed root (task-id grammar is uppercase); symlink/executable/non-regular entries are caught by findUnsafeEntries and marker checks. NOTE: Unicode-normalization/confusable segments and Windows reserved-name/trailing-dot cases are not explicitly normalized.

newProbeMatrixAtoN.name: workflow event and checkout integrity
newProbeMatrixAtoN.evidence: Actual PR #57 factory runs on 69d8d56 and recovery tip 9352e59 succeeded read-only, but the intermediate no-op commit 2d82b87 produced a FAILED run (recovery not cleanly reconciled). The workflow trusts github.event SHAs and GITHUB_WORKSPACE without verifying checked-out HEAD == trusted head.sha or that the workspace is the resolved worktree root, and (per B) runs PR-head code that a validation branch may itself have modified.

workflowValidation.judgment: Read-only and fail-closed at discovery, but it delegates to a boundary the PR head can itself modify and does not verify checkout/metadata integrity; a green run is not sufficient evidence.

correctionRequiredFindings.summary: No task-role capability profile: validation-role branches hold full implementation-write privilege (bin/lib/fixtures/workflow/lineage).
Self-authorizing validator: a PR head can weaken boundary/lineage/workflow and be checked by its own modified head code; no trusted enforcement root.
Factory governance bound to branch names, not trusted commit ancestry; force-moved/reused branches and recovery no-ops silently trusted.
Future tasks pre-authorized in FACTORY_LINEAGE; entries are branch strings only (no task id/issue/role/inventory) and self-addable.
Exact skeleton is filename-only; unsafe content substitution (safety constraints removed / production language added) passes.
Merge record accepts any/all-zero 40-hex SHA; no repository existence, main-reachability or receipt-hash linkage.
Current task setup contract/state/prompt mutable and arbitrary extra result files allowed (prefix-only result-dir authorization).
Marker enum rejects governed outcomes (VALIDATED_WITH_NONBLOCKING_NOTES); identity accepted via validation/correction task id fallback; conflicting/unknown outcome keys undetected.
History timestamps compared lexicographically (non-ISO accepted); duplicate same-state entries; no event-type/identity schema.
Workflow runs PR-head code and does not verify checked-out HEAD == trusted head.sha or GITHUB_WORKSPACE == resolved root; recovery no-op produced an inconsistent run.

nonblockingNotes: Correction V3 genuinely closed the twelve Validation-013 findings; 145/0 fixtures and the read-only PR #57 runs on the authoritative and recovery tips are green. Probes A–N are deeper, mostly NEW architectural surfaces (task-role capability, self-authorization, commit ancestry, content integrity, merge-record reachability).
G: OWNER_CLOSEOUT_REQUIRED has no separate marker-add inventory (by design); boundary and final validate jointly gate transitions.
J: owner-receipt privilege floor holds and the factory-vs-research merge distinction is respected; only post-merge lifecycle immutability and explicit all-false-matrix presence are unenforced.
L: the NUL-delimited parser matches real Git output including spaces in filenames and rename src/dst; score-range and truncation rejected.
M: symlink/executable/non-regular entries are caught; only Unicode/reserved-name confusables are unnormalized (task-id grammar is uppercase-bounded).
Authorization floor is intact; every corrections-required finding is an authorization/governance-architecture or validation-completeness gap, not a privilege escalation.
requiredCorrections: A: Introduce task-role capability profiles so validation/closeout tasks may create only their exact result files and may not modify bin/lib/fixtures/schemas/templates/README/workflow/lineage.

B: Enforce the boundary from a trusted base/bootstrap version that the PR under check cannot self-modify; reject PRs that alter the validator/lineage/workflow they are validated by without separate governance.
C: Bind factory governance to trusted commit ancestry (head descends the governed base tip; base equals the approved stack commit) and explicitly reconcile recovery no-op commits.
D: Freeze the current task's contract/state/prompt after setup and enforce an exact result-file inventory instead of whole-directory prefix authorization.
E: Make FACTORY_LINEAGE entries owner-authorized governance records carrying task id, issue/PR identity, role and allowed-file inventory; forbid a future branch from authorizing itself.
F: Verify the initial skeleton against canonical template bytes (including safety text and no-production-authorization), and reject content substitution, executable mode and symlinks.
G: Jointly require, per transition, the exact stage artifact AND the matching TASK_STATE state/history append.
H: Align marker enums with the factory's own governed outcome protocol, bind marker identity strictly to the root research task id, and reject conflicting/unknown outcome keys.

I: Verify the merge record's commit exists, is reachable from main, targets main, links the exact owner receipt by hash, and that main contains the governed task tree; reject all-zero/fabricated SHAs.
J: Require the explicit all-false non-merge authorization matrix and enforce receipt immutability across the closeout lifecycle.
K: Require a deterministic ISO-8601 history event schema with typed identity/event fields and true chronological ordering; govern same-state entries.
N: Fail closed when checked-out HEAD != trusted head.sha or GITHUB_WORKSPACE != resolved worktree root; ensure the boundary step cannot be bypassed by a head-modified workflow.
